chunks: The right of the counselor is that you act gently toward him and give ear to him.

If he presents you with the right course, you praise God, but if he does not agree with you, you show compassion toward him and make no accusations against him; you consider him to have made a mistake, and you do not take him to task for that, unless he should be deserving of accusation.
Then attach no more importance to his affair. And there is no strength save in God.

key_terms.الصَّوَابِ: The right course or correct opinion
key_terms.تَتَّهِمْنَهُ: You accuse him (of insincerity or error)
key_terms.تَصْغِيَ: You give ear or listen attentively
key_terms.تَلِينَ: You act gently or are kind
key_terms.تُعَاخِذْهُ: You take him to task or hold him accountable
key_terms.رَحِمْتَهُ: You show compassion or mercy to him
key_terms.نَّاصِحٍ: Counselor or one who gives sincere advice

ai.seo_question: How should one respond to advice from a counselor according to Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin expands the concept of nasihah by emphasizing the psychological and spiritual posture of the listener, distinguishing between mere error and insincerity.
